newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 24.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on January 24. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Academics and labour activits said the 10.07 percent increase in the minimum wage would not be sufficient for the Indonesian workers to meet basic needs.

Parliamentarians have again criticised the government's handling of non-tax revenues raised by various ministries and government agencies. They urged the government to give a full account of the use of all revenue raised from sources other than taxation since 1969.

The budgetary commission of the House of Representatives have questioned the viability of electricity generation by private firms, saying the large number of new power projects might cause an oversupply. Members of the commission say the electricity shortage might have been exaggerated by the government as a pretext to allow massive participation by private companies in power generation.
The government is likely to increase the price of cheap houses because of the hike in land and building material prices. It is still unclear when the house price will be increased.
The Indonesian ambassador to the Netherlands Soedarmanto Kadarisman said the Dutch authorities had politicised the trial of an Indonesian pilot accused of trying to smuggle 8,000 Ecstasy pills.
